# #4117: Patch: a test shows spec check failing on every kind of problem it looks for, and the check reads the dev dashboard's ruling citations too
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Every pull request runs a check that keeps the rules notes honest. Each rules decision has to name a test that runs and proves it, every rules number mentioned in the code has to have its note, and every cross-reference in the rules has to lead somewhere. The check's own tests show it failing in only a few of the ways it can.

Nothing shows that it notices the most common slip: the test that proved a decision gets renamed or deleted. Nothing shows that it notices a cross-reference that leads nowhere. A later edit to the check could quietly stop catching either one, and every pull request would still go green.

The check also never reads the dev dashboard's code, which cites six rules decisions, so a mistyped number there passes.

Once this is built, a test fails as soon as the check stops catching any one of those mistakes, and a mistyped number in the dashboard turns the check red. Players notice nothing. The maintainer and the bots get a gate they can rely on.

## Why

- `check()` (`crates/tools/src/spec.rs:1231-1405`) holds the eight rules its module header lists (`spec.rs:17-35`). It is CLAUDE.md rule 3's gate: CI runs it as `rust (checks, fuzz 200)` on every pull request that is not on the skip list (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:545-546`).
- Only three tests run `check()` over a tree:
  - rule 6, the pending paragraphs' names (`spec.rs:1741`);
  - rule 3, an R-id in an edge Worker comment (`spec.rs:1787`);
  - rule 8, the ruling markers (`spec.rs:1949`).

  Each one builds the same passing tree by hand (an R3 note and `crates/fatigue.rs`), so there are three copies of it.
- No test reaches these problem lines through `check()`:
  - **Rule 1** (`spec.rs:1238-1257`): a note with no `id`, an id that is not a ruling id, an id that belongs in another file, two notes with one id.
  - **Rule 2** (`spec.rs:1267-1284`): an empty `proven_in`, a `proven_in` path that does not exist, a file with no test that runs named after the ruling (the renamed or bare-`#[ignore]`d test), a proof that is not a test file. `proves()` has its own unit tests (`spec.rs:2032-2129`). Nothing tests that `check()` turns its `Ok(false)` or `Err` into a problem.
  - **Rule 3, Rust half** (`spec.rs:1323-1333`): a `#[test] fn r<n>_...` with no note.
  - **Rule 4** (`spec.rs:1352-1373`): whether a `[[...]]` link resolves (to a ruling, a `§` section, a note, or #3804's `[[CARDS#...]]` heading) is decided only inside `check()` and tested nowhere. The link parser and the section headings are tested (`spec.rs:2132`, `2143`); the decision is not.
  - **Rule 7**: the wiring at `spec.rs:1309` (its helper is tested at `1876`).
- Mutation testing cannot find these gaps. cargo-mutants never removes a call such as `problems.push(...)`. The three-arm `match` at `spec.rs:1278` has no wildcard arm, so no arm of it is deleted either. The tools area's mutation floor is 0 (`.github/mutants-floor.txt`).
- `check()` prints its problems and returns only their count (`spec.rs:1398`). So the existing tests can pin `1 problem(s)` but not which problem it was.
- `CITING_ROOTS` (`spec.rs:85`) is `crates`, `apps/web/src`, `apps/edge/src` and `e2e`.
  - #2854 added the edge Worker on 2026-11-02. The dev dashboard (`apps/admin`, #3085) landed on 2026-11-04 and never joined the list.
  - Seven of the dashboard's files cite R160, R192, R194, R1300000, R1310003 and R3156001: `apps/admin/src/auth.ts:5,39`, `session.ts:3`, `types.ts:78`, `testids.ts:54`, `Holdings.tsx:2`, `api.ts:128` and `auth.test.ts:112`. Each id has its note today, but a mistyped or retired one would pass.
  - The docs disagree on the list: `spec/README.md:60` names four roots, while `crates/tools/README.md:75` and CLAUDE.md rule 3 name three.

## Proposal

1. Split `check()` into two functions. `problems(root)` returns the problem lines and the counts for the ok line. `check()` prints exactly what it prints today and fails the same way.
2. Add one test helper that builds the passing tree, and switch the three existing tests to it in place of their copies.
3. Add one test per problem line of rules 1, 2, 3 (Rust names), 4 and 7. Each test makes one edit to the passing tree and asserts that `problems()` is exactly the expected line, and that the tree passes again once the edit is undone. The cases:
   - `R0003.md` with `id: R4`;
   - a second note with `id: R3`;
   - a note with no `id`, and one with `id: X3`;
   - `proven_in: []`;
   - `proven_in` naming a missing file;
   - the proving test renamed to `fn fatigue()`, and the test marked with a bare `#[ignore]`;
   - `proven_in` naming a `.md` file;
   - a `#[test] fn r<n>_x() {}` with no note;
   - in a spec note with a `## 1. ...` heading: `[[R<n>]]`, `[[§99.9]]`, `[[no-such-note]]` and `[[CARDS#Nothing]]` each fail, beside `[[R3]]`, `[[§1]]` and `[[CARDS#Pools]]`, which resolve;
   - an unresolved-ruling phrase in a code file, built with `concat!` as `UNRESOLVED_MARKERS` builds it.

   Build each unknown R-id with `format!`, as `spec.rs:1808` does, because `check` reads `spec.rs` itself.
4. Add `apps/admin/src` to `CITING_ROOTS`, with a test case where a dashboard file cites an id that has no note. Name the five roots in `spec.rs`'s header, `crates/tools/README.md`, `spec/README.md:60` and CLAUDE.md rule 3.

This is tooling and makes no rules decision, so it needs no ruling.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`: the `check()` split, `CITING_ROOTS`, the header's rule 3 line, the tests.
- `crates/tools/README.md` (the `spec check` paragraph), `spec/README.md` (Adding a ruling, line 60), CLAUDE.md rule 3's list of roots.
- SPEC: no section changes. The check enforces the process in `spec/README.md`, Adding a ruling, and CLAUDE.md rule 3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes on the tree with `apps/admin/src` read. Its ok line has the same shape; only the citation counts grow.
- [ ] Each problem line has a test that pins its text: `spec.rs:1239`, `1243`, `1247`, `1254`, `1268`, `1275`, `1280`, `1284`, `1327`, `1368` and the rule-7 `extend` at `1309`. Deleting any one of those statements makes a test fail.
- [ ] The rule 4 test holds both ways: the four broken links give one line each, and the three good ones give none.
- [ ] A dashboard file citing an id with no note gives one problem naming its `apps/admin/src/...` path and line.
- [ ] The three existing `check()` tests use the new helper and still pass. No test is deleted or `#[ignore]`d.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec::`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

## Size and risks

Small to medium, `difficulty:medium`: one Rust file carries nearly all of it. That is about 20 lines to split `check()`, about 200 lines of tests, and a few doc lines.

- Tests in one binary run in parallel under one process id, so each case needs its own temp directory name.
- `[[CARDS#...]]` resolution reads the compiled pools (`spec_cards::headings()`), so the case uses a heading that always exists (`Pools`).
- Reading `apps/admin/src` makes the gate stricter. Today's tree passes it: each of the six cited ids has its note, and no unresolved-ruling phrase is there. Nothing parses the ok line's counts.
- The `rust (checks, fuzz 200)` job runs on every pull request that is not on the skip list, so a dashboard-only pull request is checked too, and `scripts/ci-scope.sh` needs no change.
